open.summary: The document_index_units retrieval path has no EXPLAIN baseline, and Phase 5 has no query-specific plan-flip evidence
open.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): Still accurate: explain_retrieval_rpc accepts only four names and the _v2 functions are still in use. No measured regression, so P3. PRIOR DETAIL: Two Phase 5.1 deliverables are explicitly OPEN, not discharged. Re-graded P3 -> P2 versus the withdrawn request 2040d1fb, because that request understated the gap by claiming substitute coverage that does not exist. (A) NO EXPLAIN BASELINE FOR THE INDEX-UNITS PATH. public.explain_retrieval_rpc accepts exactly four names -- match_documents_for_query, match_document_chunks_text, match_document_lookup_chunks_text, match_document_table_facts_text -- and raises 22023 Unsupported retrieval RPC for anything else, proven against production for both match_document_chunks_text_v2 and match_document_index_units_hybrid_v2. For the first of those the v1 sibling match_document_chunks_text shares the owning table document_chunks and is a usable stand-in. For the second there is none: match_document_index_units_hybrid_v2 delegates to match_document_index_units_hybrid_scoped over document_index_units (supabase/schema.sql:8033-8054), and no supported RPC touches that table. document_index_units is one of the two section 1.2 outliers, so the outlier that most needed a baseline is the one that has none. (B) NO QUERY-SPECIFIC PLAN-FLIP EVIDENCE. explain_retrieval_rpc EXPLAINs `select * from public.<rpc>(...)`, so a PL/pgSQL body's inner plan is never exposed and every sample reports a single Function Scan with no index names. Plan section 5.1's 'record plan flips (seq scan -> index scan)' is therefore unanswerable through this instrument. The pg_stat_user_indexes read captured in Phase 5.1(c) is a WEAKER and DIFFERENT signal, not a substitute: idx_scan is cumulative across every workload touching the table and no before/after delta was captured around the samples, so it can prove an index is never chosen by anything but cannot prove that a given query changed plan. NEXT: one migration extending the explain_retrieval_rpc p_rpc branch list to the _v2 family (at minimum match_document_index_units_hybrid_v2 and match_document_chunks_text_v2), shipped in an approved window -- with D4 ON, merging it to main deploys it, so it needs the window and a green post-merge live-drift run. open.detail: UPDATE 2026-09-27: FIX BUILT on branch claude/repo-review-design-fixes-ao0dqw (PR #3145), NOT YET MERGED — close this row only after it lands. The 'way out' below was built: claimPhoneOverlayAddonReserve (use-phone-overlay-chrome-reserve.ts) is called by both portals and writes --phone-overlay-chrome-h inline as calc(<value in force> + <row>px) before settle, re-measures after settle, and subtracts the row on release. A production-build trace found a second cause: under reduced motion every element gets a 0.01ms transition and transition-property defaults to all, so the pad painted the stale padding-top for one frame; globals.css now sets transition-property: none on mobile-composer-reserve-pad at phone width. The required Playwright settle assertion was added (#CHPC5C test in tests/ui-phone-scroll.spec.ts): 10/10 pass on a production build, fails on the pre-fix portals. verify:full green (20027 tests); the full verify:phone-chrome run was stopped by the owner at ~342/687 and is left to CI. PREVIOUS: CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN 2026-09-20; NO LONGER PARKED. This is not a flaky test — it catches a real phone defect that also hits clinicians. The Differentials mode-nav row (49px) paints IN page flow, then ModeNavHeaderPortal moves it into the fixed phone header at ~315ms; content loses that height and every element rises 49px. usePhoneOverlayChromeReserve only republishes the measured 121px at ~423ms, so for ~110ms the whole page sits 49px too high. A press that straddles that correction lands on one control and releases on another: recorded trace shows pointerdown on the compare-open link at y 492-540, pointerup at the identical y hitting "Edit selection" because the link had moved to 443-491, and the browser retargeting the click to their common ancestor. The link never activates — no error, no navigation. scrollY is 0 throughout, so this is layout, not scrolling, and Playwright hit-target checks cannot see it because press and release were each individually on a real element. EVIDENCE: 0/41 reproductions through the repo runner (10x alone, 10x under 4 busy loops, 20x under 12, plus a full shard) — shard load is not the right kind of slowness. Under Chrome DevTools renderer throttling: 0/10 at 4x, 10/10 at 10x, 9/10 at 20x, and 0/10 at 10x when the phone chrome is allowed to settle first. That last row is the control. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW. (1) It is the PHONE click that fails, not the desktop one. tests/ui-tools.spec.ts:2928 is the test declaration; the test contains two compare-open clicks, and the URL CI recorded has no q=Pain, which matches the 390x844 phone block. Above the phone breakpoint the reserve publishes 0px and no addon row mounts, so desktop is not exposed. (2) The TO-UNBLOCK suggestion in this row does not work and is refuted: the destination "Loading presentation" role=status skeleton cannot be the settle signal, because it lives inside the destination route and only renders AFTER the URL commits. Proven by holding the destination response 20s — urlChangedAfterMs 20130, loadingSkeletonSeenAfterMs null. The "racing an unhydrated link" hypothesis is the right family but the wrong mechanism: the link is a plain next/link anchor from a Server Component, so a pre-hydration click would still navigate natively. The race is hydration-driven LAYOUT, not handlers. STILL OPEN AFTER PR #2929 — READ THIS BEFORE CLOSING THE ROW. PR #2929 (publishPhoneOverlayChromeReserveNow, called from both portals) closes this only for IN-SESSION navigation, and NOT for the cold page.goto the trace above was taken on, which is the path CI fails on. The publisher refuses to act until the reserve hook has settled a value at least once — it must, because before that responsive layout can still report the wide 200px stack (#147) and publishing that would move content twice. React runs layout effects children-first and the hook belongs to the shell, so on a cold load a portal effect ALWAYS runs before the hook has settled and the immediate publish is suppressed, every time. Established by adversarial review of #2929 and independently reproduced; pinned as failing-when-fixed cases in tests/phone-overlay-reserve-portal-wiring.dom.test.tsx, which is also the only coverage of the portals wiring at all — every case in tests/phone-overlay-chrome-reserve.dom.test.ts calls the publisher directly and would pass with both useLayoutEffect blocks deleted. A second gap: unmounting a portal does not shrink the reserve, so content sits 49px too LOW instead; a cleanup cannot simply publish, because React runs layout-effect destroys before it detaches portal children. THE WAY OUT, not yet built or verified: have the portal publish its OWN height as a delta to the reserve currently in force instead of re-measuring the whole stack. That removes the #147 exposure, and with it the settle precondition, and it gives the shrink direction naturally via the effect cleanup. It is a real change to shared phone chrome on every route and needs its own browser evidence — verify:phone-chrome plus the Playwright settle assertion docs/search-chrome-behaviour.md mandates, which was not added and is still required. OWNER DECISION PENDING on whether to do that work. MERGE VERIFICATION, carried over from the refuted request a13b357d so it is not lost: #2929 merged 2026-09-20 as commit 80cf3df6c69a, and publishPhoneOverlayChromeReserveNow is present on origin/main in globals.css, phone-header-collapse-portal.tsx and use-phone-overlay-chrome-reserve.ts. open.summary: Drift def_hash normaliser strips from any '--' to end of line, hiding 91 percent of the P03 seed function
open.detail: schema_drift_snapshot() computes a function def_hash as md5 of pg_get_functiondef with block comments, then '--[^\n]*', then all whitespace removed (supabase/migrations/20260706200000_schema_drift_snapshot.sql:89 and the 20260818090000 history-probe rewrite:97). The line-comment regex cannot tell a real comment from '--' inside a string literal. public.site_content_registry_baseline embeds the whole registry seed as a single-line dollar-quoted JSON blob, and the first '--' falls at offset 176107 inside a service URL (Next-Step---Drug-and-Alcohol-Services), so 91.1 percent of the definition - 1841007 normalised chars down to 164524 - is stripped before hashing. Measured, not inferred: replaying both the old and the new function body into a local Postgres 16 produced the identical pinned hash c2dc2183657bab3c994af7f18ddfcb9b even though the bodies differ, and that same replay reproduces the manifest value exactly for the unchanged body, so the control is sound. Consequence: check:drift and the post-merge live-drift workflow cannot see a change to that function's seed data after the first '--'. Every other function loses only genuine comments, which is the intended behaviour. A fix has to distinguish a comment from a literal - dollar-quoted bodies could be hashed unstripped, or the strip applied only outside string literals - and it changes def_hash for every function, so it needs a manifest regeneration in the same change.

open.summary: site_content_release_records_immutable is not 'enable always', so session_replication_role = replica bypasses the freeze's only structural protection
open.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): Two of three gaps closed by 20260916190000_seal_bootstrap_release_and_drop_per_read_digest.sql (#2855: enable-always insert/truncate triggers, per-read digest removed). Remaining: the one-line enable-always promotion of site_content_release_records_immutable, deliberately left out of that migration. The sequencing advice is moot. PRIOR DETAIL: READ FROM THE SCHEMA ON 2026-09-16, NOT EXPLOITED OR TESTED. supabase/schema.sql:12722-12724 creates site_content_release_records_immutable as an ordinary row trigger (before update or delete ... execute function guard_site_content_immutable_row). PostgreSQL does not fire an ordinary trigger when session_replication_role = 'replica', so a session that sets that GUC can UPDATE or DELETE rows of the frozen epoch-zero release with nothing raising. That is not a theoretical technique in this repository: scripts/check-site-content-control-plane.mjs:889-894 uses exactly it against a sibling table. TWO FURTHER GAPS IN THE SAME SEAL: the trigger covers only UPDATE and DELETE, so nothing prevents a row being INSERTED into a retained bootstrap release (it need only satisfy site_content_release_records_check1), and TRUNCATE is a statement-level event a row trigger never sees. Until the catalogue read-latency migration lands, the per-read bootstrap digest recomputation is the only thing that detects an inserted row, and it detects it after the fact — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. HOW MUCH THIS MATTERS, stated honestly: setting session_replication_role needs the same superuser or postgres privilege an attacker would need to write the rows anyway, and such an attacker could equally replace the digest function. So the value here is against ACCIDENT — a half-applied migration, a bad replay, a partial restore, or a script that sets the GUC for an unrelated reason and then touches this table — not against a determined adversary. THE FIX: 'alter table public.site_content_release_records enable always trigger site_content_release_records_immutable', plus an 'enable always' before-insert trigger restricted to the retained bootstrap release ids and an 'enable always' before-truncate statement trigger. All transactional, no index build. SEQUENCE IT WITH the read-latency migration, which needs the same seal to justify removing the per-read digest; doing it separately means doing the same CREATE TRIGGER lock twice. GATE: SQL, so it ships as a new forward migration and needs an approved merge window. RUN check:site-content-control-plane in Docker FIRST — its own fixtures rely on session_replication_role on a sibling table, and an 'enable always' trigger on this one must be proven not to break them before merging.

open.summary: site_content_canonical_json is recursive plpgsql, so release activation will slow the same way the read path did once a release exceeds a couple of thousand records
open.detail: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): The row's own action is 'nothing yet', so P3. site_content_canonical_json is untouched. PRIOR DETAIL: READ FROM THE SQL ON 2026-09-16, NOT MEASURED. site_content_canonical_json (supabase/schema.sql:12746) is a recursive plpgsql function: one invocation per JSON node, and a string_agg subquery over jsonb_each or jsonb_array_elements at every container. It defines EVERY fingerprint in the site-content control plane — release digest, contentHash, publicationVersion, governance and lineage hashes, plan and receipt identities — and is reimplemented in JS and pinned by tests/site-content-p03-baseline.test.ts, so it cannot be rewritten without invalidating stored digests across the live database. Measured proxy for its cost: the 843-record epoch-zero freeze canonicalises to 9,522,923 bytes across 164,820 JSON nodes (55,103 containers), i.e. ~165k plpgsql invocations and ~55k planned aggregate subqueries per pass, and two such passes per HTTP request cost about four seconds against live — see docs/audit/2026-09-16-catalogue-read-latency.md. The read path is being fixed by removing the calls. The WRITE path cannot be: site_content_dynamic_state_digest, site_content_release_digest, stage_site_content_sync_event, activate_site_content_release and rollback_site_content_release all canonicalise the full release by design and must keep doing so. Today that is tolerable because activation is rare and operator-driven. It scales linearly in node count, so a release of 2,000+ records makes activation slow in exactly the same way, and an activation that exceeds its statement timeout fails a publication rather than a page view. WHAT TO DO: nothing yet — this is a recorded scaling limit, not a defect. BEFORE the catalogue grows materially past the freeze, time one activation against a realistic release on a local Postgres (npm run check:site-content-control-plane already replays the control plane in Docker) and record the node-count-to-seconds curve, so the ceiling is known before an operator hits it mid-publication. DO NOT rewrite site_content_canonical_json to a set-based or C-backed equivalent as a performance fix: any byte-level difference changes every stored fingerprint, and a C extension cannot be installed by migration on Supabase.

Commits: 1629 published commits carry the records, 1335 of them on origin/main - not the 3 the ruling recorded and every later restatement repeated. THE COMMIT FIGURE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because it is what the ruling's own argument rests on: 'publishing a repository publishes its history'. Every earlier count used git log -S, the pickaxe, which finds commits where a string's PRESENCE CHANGES, not commits whose TREE CONTAINS it. There are only two distinct versions of src/components/ward-management/ward-patients-seed.ts in the entire repository and BOTH hold the eight records, so every commit carrying that file exposes them. The 12 came from searching UM100001, the first record of eight, missing four files carrying only one of the other seven. A privacy count is easy to take against one specimen, one branch, or one kind of change, and every such shortcut truncates - toward making publication look safer. Measure containment, not change, and pin the SHA. open.summary: A Playwright run whose own web server fails to start silently reuses another server and reports green
open.detail: Observed 2026-09-20 while writing tests/ui-patient-number-field.spec.ts. The agent running scripts/run-playwright.mjs had its own webServer fail to start because a concurrent session already held the port; the runner did not stop. It proceeded against THAT other server and reported a green pass. The run was re-done cleanly afterwards and the reported result is sound, but the hazard is not the individual run — it is that a browser gate can report success without ever exercising the tree it claims to test. This is the same class of failure as a gate piped into tail (exit code masked) and as CLINICAL_HAZARD_CONTROLS_PASS printing while a named proof file had been emptied: a signal that cannot fail is worse than no signal, because it is trusted. It matters more here than in most repos because verification evidence is quoted verbatim into PR bodies and the ledger, so a contaminated run propagates as fact. NEXT: make Playwright webServer startup failure fatal rather than falling back to an already-listening port — either set reuseExistingServer:false for CI/agent runs, or have run-playwright.mjs confirm the server it connects to is the one it started (the repo already has /api/local-project-id for exactly this identity question, used by npm run ensure). Add a contract test that a failed server start exits non-zero. Note npm run ensure already solves the adjacent problem correctly and is the pattern to copy.

open.summary: Two Firefox failures survive the 2026-09-20 triage: the document-viewer hit counter and the tools Forms panel, both a click whose state change never lands
open.detail: Read the Playwright trace from the failing run BEFORE proposing any fix; playwright.config.ts sets trace: retain-on-failure so it exists, and its After-DOM snapshot of the click answers this in minutes. THE TWO: (1) ui-smoke.spec.ts "search regressions avoid fetch errors and open viewer hits @critical" - after clicking Next document search hit, "Hit 2 of 2" never appears (element NOT FOUND, not hidden); (2) ui-tools.spec.ts "tool links point to the expected in-app modes" - the Forms complementary panel resolves to zero elements, on the 4th of 6 loop passes, while Services with an identical /?mode=<id> href passes. SAME SHAPE, so probably one shared Firefox cause. RULED OUT by two independent agent reads, do not re-derive: text split across elements (Playwright elementText flattens descendants and JSX/SSR comment separators); a collapsed <details> or any CSS cause (a hidden node still matches, and would report hidden not not-found - no stylesheet removes a node from the DOM); scrollIntoView/smooth scroll (suite-wide reducedMotion: reduce makes resolveScrollBehavior return auto); keyboard/focus; a click intercepted by the fixed composer (Playwright's hit-target interceptor blocks and retries, failing AT the click); Forms-specific data or markup (tools-catalog.ts Forms and Services are the same shape, and DetailActions renders the href link unconditionally). LEADING CANDIDATES: for (1), the handler firing zero times or twice - with exactly 2 hits, (i+d+2)%2 returns to 0 either way - with the exclusive-accordion open-attribute fight at source-panels.tsx:1063 as a plausible Gecko-specific trigger; for (2), the panel's hardcoded aria-labelledby id resolving against a hidden duplicate page root (the #093 failure mode visibleByTestId exists for), or the bare focus() at tools-search-results-page.tsx:470 scrolling late. NEITHER IS PROVEN. Why: Why it matters - if the click genuinely no-ops, a Firefox user cannot page through document search hits at all, which is a clinical reading path; if it double-fires it is a harness artefact and the test should assert the active chunk id rather than a modulo-2 counter. Context: Six Firefox failures in main run 35503893104; four fixed in PRs #2932 and #2933, these two left. Parent row #9Z197J. Owner: unknown - depends on what the trace shows. open.summary: Caller IP addresses are stored as unsalted truncated SHA-256 with no retention limit in api_rate_limit_subjects
open.detail: anonymousApiSubjectKey (src/lib/public-api-access.ts) derives the rate-limit subject as the prefix anon: plus the first 32 hex characters of an unsalted SHA-256 of the trusted proxy IP, and stores it in api_rate_limit_subjects.subject_key. The IPv4 address space is small enough that an unsalted hash of it is brute-forced in seconds, so these rows are PSEUDONYMISED, not anonymised, and should be classified as personal information rather than treated as opaque. Separately, and unlike rag_queries, the table has no purge function and no retention window, so rows persist indefinitely (supabase/migrations/20260704000000_api_rate_limit_subjects.sql enables row level security and grants select/insert/update/delete to service_role only). NOT AN EXPOSURE: RLS is on and only service_role reaches it, so a stranger cannot read it. This is a retention and classification matter, which is why it was deferred rather than fixed on the day. NEXT ACTION: two separable decisions. open.summary: Owner design decision: first publication versus adoption for the site catalogue (blocks #HTZPQ8)
open.detail: OWNER DECISION 2026-09-25: first publication, not adoption. The 222 owner-scoped service rows and 54 forms go public through the administrator first-publication flow in owner-approved batches, each batch clinically signed off (the 17 newest service records need sign-off before they can publish). Do not relax the reconciliation triage to make adoption pass. Next action: design and build the first-publication path; it touches site_content tables, so any migration follows the Supabase merge-is-deploy rule. PRIOR DETAIL: REVIEW 2026-09-25 (offline audit of current main; no provider access): The 'smaller, separate' part is fixed: a27fc99a9 adds a not_comparable verdict with an honest message and seven tests, and docs/site-content-publication-handover.md section 2.5 warns that steps 2-3 cannot complete. What remains is the owner decision between first publication and adoption. PRIOR DETAIL: WHAT HAPPENS. scripts/build-site-content-reconciliation-plan.ts, run against a fresh operator export (843 records, activeReleaseId e4a1dd29, initialized=false, expected=actual=843), reports: owner rows 222, logical groups 222, published groups 843, groups not published 3, TRIAGE SNAPSHOTS 0, needs owner review 222, adoptable 0, identical duplicates 0. It then refuses, telling the operator that 222 groups diverge from the published snapshot and that choosing between them is a clinical judgement. WHY THAT MESSAGE IS MISLEADING. Nothing diverged. buildRegistryReconciliationReport can only mark a group adoptable when canonicalCandidate returns a candidate, and canonicalCandidate delegates to reconcileCanonicalPublicSiteContent, which requires ALL FOUR of publicationState='published', renderedByPublicSite=true, explicitlyReconciled=true and rowOwnerId=null. Measured on live: clinical_registry_records has 222 service rows and 54 form rows, ALL with a non-null owner_id; site_content_publications has 0 rows; site_content_public_records has 0 rows. So no candidate can satisfy those conditions in this state, no triage snapshot is ever built, and every group falls through to divergent_requires_administrator_review by construction. The count 222-of-222 is an artefact of the state, not a measurement of drift. WHY IT MATTERS. The handover (docs/site-content-publication-handover.md) tells the owner the order is export, then reconciliation plan, then the administrator records it. Step 2 cannot produce output, so the owner would follow the documented order and hit a refusal that blames the corpus. Worse, the refusal is the kind that invites someone to 'fix' it by relaxing the triage, which would mark owner-scoped rows canonical for a clinical publication - exactly the judgement the script exists to refuse. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED, and it is a design decision rather than a bug fix. The reconciliation/adoption path is built for rows that are ALREADY public and whose identity is settled; it adopts them into the control plane. This corpus has never published anything through the control plane at all - the epoch-zero freeze lives only in site_content_release_records. So the question to settle before any more tooling is whether initial adoption is the right mechanism here, or whether these 222 owner-scoped service rows need a first-publication path that makes them public and unowned through the administrator flow. Do NOT resolve it by loosening reconcileCanonicalPublicSiteContent. SMALLER, SEPARATE: the planner should say what it actually found. A refusal that reports 'triage snapshots 0' alongside 'needs owner review 222' should state that the two together mean nothing was comparable, not that 222 things disagreed.

open.summary: verify:phone-chrome and verify:ui cannot go green in a cloud sandbox: three failures are the unpinned Chromium, not the code
open.detail: Established 2026-09-20 by running the three failures against a clean origin/main worktree (aef181f55) with the same environment, and reading the saved failure snapshots. They reproduce identically on main, so they are a property of the sandbox, not of any branch. ROOT CAUSE, found rather than guessed: the only installable browser here is /opt/pw-browsers/chromium = chromium-1194 = Chromium 141.0.7390.37, because cdn.playwright.dev is 403 under the egress policy and the revision Playwright 1.63.0 pins is 1243 / Chromium 153. (1) tests/ui-smoke.spec.ts "document frame stretches the canvas owner at phone and desktop" and "document viewer puts the PDF preview first with pinned evidence after it on mobile" both fail with getByTestId(pdf-canvas-scroll).locator(canvas) "element(s) not found". The error-context snapshot shows the viewer in its error state with the text "this[#re].getOrInsertComputed is not a function" and a Retry preview button. pdfjs-dist@6.3.289 calls Map.prototype.getOrInsertComputed, a V8 addition Chromium 141 does not have, so pdf.js throws during load and no canvas is ever created. The demo PDFs and cover images are all present; nothing is missing from the fixture. (2) tests/ui-pwa.spec.ts "has a browser-valid manifest, installable icons, and a root worker" fails with installability error "in-incognito" — Chromium refusing because every Playwright BrowserContext is off-the-record. Every other assertion in that test (manifest URL, manifest contents, all icon probes, service-worker scope/state/controller) passes first. CONSEQUENCE FOR AGENTS: three failures out of ~798 passing is the FLOOR for a chromium browser gate in this environment, on any branch. Do not read it as a branch signal, and do not "fix" a test to make it pass here. CI runs the pinned browser and the Production UI chromium shards are green on recent main (7936c3f9, cfb5ed90, and shard 3 on aef181f55). NOT ESTABLISHED: per-test CI granularity, because gh run view --log is Forbidden here (results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com); only job-level green was read. That Chromium 153 stops reporting in-incognito is an inference from CI being green, not a direct observation. TO UNBLOCK: either allowlist cdn.playwright.dev so the pinned revision installs, or teach the browser gate to recognise this known trio and report them as environment-floor rather than failures.
